content_ta: Intuit நிறுவனத்தின் Chairman மற்றும் CEO-வான Sasan Goodarzi, வருவாய் குறித்த கூட்டத்தில் பேசுகையில், செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவு கருவிகள் கண்டுபிடிப்புகளுக்கான புதிய நுழைவாயில்களாக மாறி வருவதாகத் தெரிவித்தார். வாடிக்கையாளர்கள் தாங்கள் விரும்பும் இடங்களில் வேலை செய்ய அனுமதிப்பதே நிறுவனத்தின் முக்கிய வியூகமாகும் என்று அவர் குறிப்பிட்டார்.

title: FDIC Proposal Details How Banks Can Pay FinTechs in Deposit Deals
summary:
The Federal Deposit Insurance Corp.’s Nov. 17 proposal implements a provision of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act that lets eligible banks exclude certain custodial deposits from their brokered deposit totals. content: The Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. has released a proposal that outlines how banks can classify certain custodial deposits under a housing act provision. title: VanEck drops Gemini as custodian of its bitcoin, ether and SOL ETFs
summary: Coinbase Custody will continue serving all three funds after Gemini's contracts end in February.
content: VanEck has dropped Gemini as the custodian for its bitcoin, ether, and SOL exchange-traded funds. Following the termination of these contracts in February, Coinbase Custody will step in to manage all three funds moving forward. This change impacts the custody arrangements for these specific digital asset investment products offered by VanEck.
content_ta: VanEck தனது bitcoin, ether மற்றும் SOL ETF-களுக்கான காவாவாளராக (custodian) செயல்பட்ட Gemini நிறுவனத்துடனான ஒப்பந்தத்தை ரத்து செய்துள்ளது. பிப்ரவரி மாதத்துடன் இந்த ஒப்பந்தங்கள் முடிவுக்கு வரும் நிலையில், Coinbase Custody நிறுவனம் இந்த மூன்று நிதிகளையும் தொடர்ந்து நிர்வகிக்கும் என்று அறிவிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: Bitcoin hits four-month low after Anthropic's IPO as tech stocks wilt
summary: Bitcoin remains under pressure after Anthropic's IPO as Nasdaq futures dip below their 200-day average.
content: Bitcoin dropped to a four-month low following Anthropic's initial public offering. The leading cryptocurrency faced renewed downward pressure as broader technology stocks weakened and Nasdaq futures dipped below their crucial 200-day average, reflecting a cautious market sentiment.
content_ta: Anthropic-ன் IPO வெளியீட்டைத் தொடர்ந்து Bitcoin நான்கு மாதக் குறைந்தபட்ச சரிவைச் சந்தித்தது. தொழில்நுட்பப் பங்குகள் பலவீனமடைந்ததாலும், Nasdaq ஃபியூச்சர்ஸ் அதன் முக்கிய 200 நாள் சராசரிக்குக் கீழே குறைந்ததாலும் முன்னணி கிரிப்டோகரன்சி கடுமையான அழுத்தத்தை எதிர்கொண்டது.

title: Institutions pile back into US Bitcoin ETFs in Q3 after selling streak
summary: Asset managers added the equivalent of 49,229 Bitcoin to their US Bitcoin ETF holdings in the third quarter, reversing three quarters of net selling.
content: Institutional asset managers significantly increased their exposure to US Bitcoin ETFs during the third quarter. After experiencing three consecutive quarters of net selling, these large financial institutions added a substantial amount of Bitcoin to their holdings, signaling a renewed interest in the digital asset market through regulated exchange-traded funds.
content_ta: மூன்றாவது காலாண்டில் நிறுவன முதலீட்டாளர்கள் US Bitcoin ETF-களில் தங்கள் முதலீட்டை மீண்டும் அதிகரித்துள்ளனர். தொடர்ந்து மூன்று காலாண்டுகளாக விற்பனையில் ஈடுபட்டு வந்த இந்த பெரிய நிதி நிறுவனங்கள், தற்போது குறிப்பிடத்தக்க அளவில் Bitcoin-ஐ தங்கள் holdings-ல் சேர்த்துள்ளன, இது ஒழுங்குபடுத்தப்பட்ட exchange-traded funds மூலம் டிஜிட்டல் சொத்து சந்தை மீதான புதிய ஆர்வத்தைக் குறிக்கிறது.

title: Coinbase backs CFTC proposal to distinguish prediction market contracts from gambling
summary: Coinbase said event contracts already qualify as swaps under the CEA and that explicit inclusion would provide greater regulatory certainty.
content: Cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase has voiced support for a proposal by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission regarding prediction market contracts. Coinbase stated that these event contracts already qualify as swaps under the Commodity Exchange Act. The company believes that explicit regulatory inclusion would provide much-needed certainty for the market.
content_ta: கிரிப்டோகரன்சி எக்ஸ்சேஞ்ச் ஆன Coinbase, CFTC-ன் கணிப்பு சந்தை ஒப்பந்தங்கள் தொடர்பான பரிந்துெரைக்கு தனது ஆதரவைத் தெரிவித்துள்ளது. இந்த நிகழ்வு ஒப்பந்தங்கள் ஏற்கனவே Commodity Exchange Act-ன் கீழ் ஸ்வாப்களாகத் தகுதிபெறுகின்றன என்று Coinbase கூறியது. தெளிவான ஒழுங்குமுறைச் சேர்க்கை சந்தைக்குத் தேவையான நிச்சயத்தன்மையை வழங்கும் என்று நிறுவனம் நம்புகிறது.

Tether நிறுவனம் தங்கத்தின் இருப்பை அதிகரிப்பதிலும் பொதுப் பங்குகளில் முதலீடு செய்வதன் மூலமும் தனது போர்ட்ஃபோலியோவை விரிவுபடுத்தியுள்ள போதிலும், இதுபோன்ற உயர்-ரிஸ்க் சொத்துக்களின் அதிகரிப்பு கவலைக்குரியது என்று ஆய்வாளர்கள் எச்சரிக்கின்றனர்.

title: This Bitcoin miner sold 267 BTC to clear $22 million debt. It still may not survive
summary: PowerCompute had its lender sell 267 pledged bitcoin in September, wiping out most of its debt, and ended the month with about $650,000 in cash and a going-concern warning.
content: Bitcoin miner PowerCompute sold 267 pledged BTC in September to clear $22 million in debt. Despite wiping out most of its financial liabilities, the company ended the month with only about $650,000 in cash and still faces a serious going-concern warning, raising doubts about whether it will ultimately survive.
content_ta: Bitcoin miner PowerCompute, செப்டம்பர் மாதத்தில் தனது $22 மில்லியன் கடனை அடைப்பதற்காக 267 pledged BTC-ஐ விற்றது. இதன் மூலம் தனது பெரும்பாலான கடன் சுமையை தீர்த்த போதிலும், அந்த மாதத்தின் இறுதியில் நிறுவனத்திடம் சுமார் $650,000 ரொக்கம் மட்டுமே இருந்தது. மேலும், இது நிறுவனம் தொடர்ந்து இயங்குவதில் சந்தேகம் எழுப்பும் வகையில் ஒரு going-concern எச்சரிக்கையையும் எதிர்கொண்டுள்ளது.

title: Big money bought a net $4 billion of bitcoin funds in Q3, ending 9 months of selling

title: Cardano’s $5M conference budget has a $1M problem — Details!

title: SoFi Study Reveals How Crypto Is Becoming Part of the Bigger Financial Picture
summary:
SoFi Technologies, Inc., the everything app for digital financial services, today released “From Side Quest to Financial Strategy,” a national report exploring the growing role of crypto in people's financial lives. Gen Z is leading the shift, with nearly two-thirds seeing crypto as a financial opportunity previous generations didn't have. 21% own cryptocurrency, seven times the rate of Boomers. The findings also challenge long-held investor stereotypes and highlight interest in managing crypto alongside everyday banking and investing.
“Gen Z has come of age in a world where money is already digital, so it’s natural that they’re pushing the boundaries of the traditional, one-size-fits-all approach to building wealth,” said Natalie Brunell, host of Coin Stories, author of Bitcoin Is for Everyone and contributor to SoFi’s On The Block. “What people are asking for now is not just access to new tools, but the education and connected experience to understand how they fit together and support their broader financial goals.”
The value of having your finances connected goes beyond convenience. As people explore new ways to manage and build wealth, keeping track of their money matters more than ever. In fact, more than one in five respondents estimate they've lost or missed out on $1,000 or more over the past year because their finances are spread across multiple platforms.
“People have more opportunities than ever to grow their money, and digital assets are opening new possibilities for how they invest and build wealth,” said Brian Walsh, CFP®, PhD and Head of Advice & Planning at SoFi. “But having more financial options is only valuable if you can make the most of them. At SoFi, we're bringing banking, investing and crypto together so members can see their full financial picture, explore new opportunities with confidence and make smarter money moves to achieve their ambitions.”
The trends shaping the next era of money:
The future of money is connected. Nearly two-thirds (63%) of crypto investors say integrating crypto with their primary bank would make them more likely to invest more. Among Gen Z, 43% say bank integration would make them more likely to invest, compared with 9% of Boomers.
Gen Z is rewriting the wealth-building playbook. More than one in five (21%) see crypto as a path to generational wealth, compared with just 8% of the general population. Gen Z is also more likely to own crypto (21%) than an employer-sponsored retirement plan (16%), and represents nearly one-third (31%) of SoFi’s crypto members.
Crypto curiosity is opening the door to new investors. More than half of Americans (52%) say they should know more about crypto, including 63% of Gen Z. Even among current crypto investors, 82% say there's more they want to learn.
Debunking the 'Tech Bro' Myth. Nearly one-third of Gen Z discuss crypto often or sometimes in daily life (31%). Black and Hispanic respondents are more than twice as likely (22%) as White respondents (9%) to own it, while women are nearly as likely as men to be crypto-curious (12% vs. 13%).
America's crypto landscape is anything but one-size-fits-all. Miami leads the 10 cities surveyed in crypto ownership (20%), while New York City outpaces tech hub San Francisco (17% vs. 13%). Kansas City sits at the other end of the spectrum, with just 5% invested.
SoFi members are already bringing crypto into their broader financial lives. Nearly all SoFi Crypto members (97%) also use another SoFi product, including SoFi Money checking or savings accounts (85%) and SoFi Invest (64%). “I’ve started moving my outside crypto holdings into SoFi because having my accounts together in one place makes managing my finances easier,” said a SoFi member.
One year after becoming the first nationally chartered bank to launch crypto trading, SoFi continues to bring the best of banking and crypto together in one app. Members can buy, sell and hold more than 40 cryptocurrencies alongside banking and investing. SoFi Earn (SOFIE) deposit token offers 4.40% APY on eligible FDIC-insured deposits, while SoFiUSD stablecoin enables 24/7 on-chain transactions. Together, these innovations make digital assets part of members’ broader financial lives, with the trust and safeguards of a bank.

content_ta: Cathie Wood-யின் ARK Invest நிறுவனம், Anthropic நிறுவனத்தின் Nasdaq தொடக்கத்தின்போது 90 மில்லியன் டாலர் மதிப்புள்ள பங்குகளை வாங்கியுள்ளது. இந்த முதலீடு ARK-ன் ஆறு ஃபண்டுகளில் பரவலாக மேற்கொள்ளப்பட்டது. அதேவேளையில், சிப் தயாரிப்பாளரான Nvidia நிறுவனத்தில் நிலவும் தலைமைத்துவ குழப்பங்களுக்கு மத்தியில், அதன் பங்குகளில் சிலவற்றை இந்நிறுவனம் விற்றுள்ளது.

title: CryptoUK Urges FCA Not to Treat DeFi Devs as Regulated by Default
summary: The UK crypto trade group broadly backed the regulator's proposed perimeter guidance, but warned that parts of it go further than the law.
content: CryptoUK, the UK crypto trade group, has urged the Financial Conduct Authority not to treat decentralized finance developers as regulated by default. While backing most of the regulator's proposed perimeter guidance, the group warned that certain aspects extend beyond current legal boundaries, raising concerns for the developing sector.
content_ta: UK-ஐச் சேர்ந்த crypto வர்த்தக அமைப்பான CryptoUK, DeFi டெவலப்பர்களை இயல்பாகவே ஒழுங்குமுறைக்கு உட்பட்டவர்களாகக் கருத வேண்டாம் என FCA-வை வலியுறுத்தியுள்ளது. ஒழுங்குமுறை அதிகாரியின் முன்மொழியப்பட்ட வழிகாட்டுதல்களை அமைப்பு ஆதரித்த போதிலும், சில பகுதிகள் சட்ட வரம்புகளை மீறுவதாக எச்சரித்துள்ளது.

title: Senate passes ‘Death Bets Act’ to ban prediction market contracts tied to death and war
summary: The Death Bets Act, which now heads to the House, would ban prediction market contracts tied to death, terrorism, assassination, and war.
content: The Senate has successfully passed the Death Bets Act, a new legislative measure designed to prohibit prediction market contracts tied to sensitive and harmful events such as death, terrorism, assassination, and war. Having cleared the Senate, the bill now moves forward to the House for further review and consideration.
content_ta: மரணம், பயங்கரவாதம், படுகொலை மற்றும் போர் போன்ற விவகாரங்கள் தொடர்பான கணிப்பு சந்தை ஒப்பந்தங்களை தடை செய்வதற்காக உருவாக்கப்பட்ட Death Bets Act மசோதாவை Senate நிறைவேற்றியுள்ளது. Senate-ல் நிறைவேற்றப்பட்டுள்ள இந்த மசோதா, அடுத்த கட்ட பரிசீலனைக்காக House-க்கு அனுப்பப்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: Coinbase opens crypto options in a market that accounted for just 2% of Deribit’s trading
summary:
USDC options made up about 2% of Deribit’s October options turnover. Two matched calls show how displayed size can differ by side and settlement currency.
Read the full story on CryptoSlate
Understand the crypto stories that matter and what to watch next. Get The Catalyst in your inbox
content: Coinbase has launched crypto options trading, entering a market where similar USDC options previously accounted for only about 2% of Deribit’s October turnover. Market data and matched calls illustrate how displayed size can vary significantly by side and settlement currency as competition in the derivatives sector grows.
content_ta: Coinbase தனது crypto options வர்த்தகத்தைத் தொடங்கியுள்ளது. Deribit-இன் அக்டோபர் மாத வர்த்தகத்தில் இதே போன்ற USDC options சுமார் 2% மட்டுமே பங்களித்திருந்த சந்தையில் தற்போது நுழைந்துள்ளது. derivatives துறையில் போட்டி அதிகரித்து வரும் நிலையில், சந்தை தரவுகள் மற்றும் பொருத்தப்பட்ட calls ஆகியவை settlement currency அடிப்படையில் எவ்வாறு மாறுபடுகின்றன என்பதைக் காட்டுகின்றன.

title: Bitcoin Crash Could Hit the US Harder Than Other Countries: Peter Schiff
summary: The economist also questioned how long Michael Saylor can keep buying STRC shares as falling BTC prices put pressure on Strategy's finances.
content: Economist Peter Schiff warned that a Bitcoin market crash could impact the United States more severely than other nations. He also raised concerns about Michael Saylor's ongoing ability to purchase STRC shares as declining BTC prices create financial pressure for the company.
content_ta: Bitcoin சரிவு மற்ற நாடுகளை விட United States-ஐ அதிகம் பாதிக்கக்கூடும் என்று economist Peter Schiff எச்சரித்துள்ளார். மேலும், falling BTC விலைகள் காரணமாக Strategy-யின் நிதிநிலையில் அழுத்தம் ஏற்பட்டுள்ள நிலையில், Michael Saylor-ஆல் தொடர்ந்து எவ்வளவு காலம் STRC shares வாங்க முடியும் என்பது குறித்தும் அவர் கேள்வி எழுப்பியுள்ளார்.

summary: That’s two Asian regulators now watching the exchange.
content: Hyperliquid traders are placing bets related to Anthropic following news that the platform has been added to Hong Kong's warning list. title: 'Rich Dad' Author Robert Kiyosaki Calls Bitcoin Drop Below $62,000 a Gift, Prepares to Buy More
summary: Amid a November crypto and metals sell-off, Robert Kiyosaki says “strong hands” wait to buy as Bitcoin drops under $62,000.

title: BMO Demonstrates Quantum Utility in Machine Learning Application Using IBM Quantum Computers
summary:
BMO announced it has demonstrated quantum utility in a machine learning application using IBM quantum computers, meaning the work was performed reliably at a scale beyond what exact traditional computing methods can practically reproduce. The work explores how quantum computing could help AI models identify which information matters most in complex datasets, potentially allowing them to uncover useful insights with less data than traditional approaches.
Over time, that capability could have applications across banking, including more accurate client modeling, improved risk assessment and detection, and more personalized client experiences.
Developed in collaboration with the Democritus University of Thrace (DUTH), using IBM quantum computers, including the latest IBM Quantum Nighthawk r2 processor, and reviewed by IBM's quantum research team, the achievement marks an important step in bringing quantum computing closer to practical use in financial services and ultimately creating value for clients and shareholders.
This project is part of BMO's broader strategy to responsibly apply quantum technologies to AI and machine learning applications.
"Demonstrating quantum utility is an important milestone for BMO and an exciting step forward for the broader financial services industry," said Kristin Milchanowski, Chief AI and Quantum Officer and Director, BMO Institute for Applied Artificial Intelligence & Quantum. "While we remain in the early stages of application development, these projects show how quantum computing can help solve business problems in new ways. This work builds on years of research, collaboration and innovation focused on identifying practical applications that create value for clients, employees and shareholders."
As an early investor in quantum research and one of a small number of global financial institutions applying quantum computing to real-world challenges, BMO continues to focus on practical and responsible innovations that create value for clients.
Applying Quantum Computing to Real Business Challenges
The application built by BMO and DUTH reimagines machine learning feature selection by adapting the Proxy Quantum Games framework, shifting it from a traditional classical statistical problem into a dynamic, quantum strategic game. Each feature of the dataset is a "player." A feature, or "player," scores high when it moves together with the applications' target (the model outcome variable), and low when it is uninformative or repeats other, unimportant features. The scores rank the features. This quantum game-based feature selection processes all of this on a quantum computer, and the resulting method produces results with similar quality, while only requiring one to two orders of magnitude fewer samples than traditional feature selection techniques.
"I'm excited to see BMO's progress toward real-world quantum use cases in the financial services industry, using our quantum computers to explore novel algorithmic approaches," said Scott Crowder, Vice President, IBM Quantum Adoption and Business Development.
Advancing Practical Quantum Innovation
BMO joined the IBM Quantum Network in February 2025 and continues to invest in quantum research, talent development and real-world applications. Through partnerships with the Chicago Quantum Exchange and Quantum Industry Canada, BMO is advancing practical applications of quantum computing across financial services. BMO also launched the BMO Institute for Applied Artificial Intelligence & Quantum, an enterprise-wide Centre of Excellence focused on the responsible application and governance of AI and the advancement of quantum capabilities.
"At BMO, innovation is about translating emerging technologies into meaningful business impact," said Steve Tennyson, Chief Technology and Operations Officer, BMO. "This milestone reflects years of investment in innovation, quantum computing, artificial intelligence and strategic partnerships. It demonstrates how BMO is turning emerging technologies into practical solutions that help clients improve decision-making and support long-term growth."
BMO's progress is also reflected in the 2026 Quantum Index Finance ranking, an independent benchmark of enterprise quantum readiness. BMO ranked ninth among financial institutions globally and is the highest-ranking Canadian commercial bank in the index. The ranking measures institutions in the areas of quantum workforce, research and development, and adoption.
Additionally, BMO was recently recognized by Evident AI as one of the world's top 20 banks in AI and ranked #2 among 50 banks for AI use-case outcomes - the highest-ranking Canadian bank in the category. BMO also achieved the top ranking in the Responsible AI Process indicator group, reflecting its approach to governance, risk management, employee training and operational controls.

title: Consumers Aren’t Ready for AI Agents to Make Purchases on Their Behalf, Signicat Reveals Ahead of Black Friday
summary:
Consumers welcome AI advice, but 69% draw the line at AI making purchases for them.
New research from Signicat shows that European consumers are open to AI supporting their decisions, but far less willing to hand over control. While 65% welcome AI assistance with tasks such as finding information, completing forms or exploring financial products, 69% are uncomfortable letting AI make purchases on their behalf. Only 19% would trust AI to make a small, low-value purchase, dropping to just 8% for a high-value one.
The findings of Signicat’s research suggest that growing AI adoption should not be confused with a willingness to hand over control. When consumers were asked what would make them more comfortable with AI opening a financial product on their behalf, 39% of consumers pointed to keeping final approval, while 32% wanted the ability to override the AI at any point.
“Consumers are clearly open to AI making their lives easier. But there's a big difference between asking AI for help and giving it the authority to act on your behalf. (...)"
Emma Bauer, Chief Product Officer at Signicat
“Customers want a copilot, not an autopilot,” said Emma Bauer, Chief Product Officer at Signicat. “Consumers are clearly open to AI making their lives easier. But there's a big difference between asking AI for help and giving it the authority to act on your behalf. Our research shows that 69% of European consumers are uncomfortable letting AI make purchases for them today. And when it comes to spending money, using someone's identity or signing agreements, control really matters.The challenge for retailers and payment providers is to build that trust – making it clear what AI is allowed to do, and ensuring customers stay in control of the decisions that matter.”
The push towards AI-assisted shopping is also taking place againtst a backdrop of rising identity fraud. Signicat’s previous The Battle in the Dark research, including a dedicated analysis of the payments and fintech sector, found that 67% of payment and fintech companies had experienced an increase in identity fraud attempts, while 54% reported a rise in more successful attacks.
With account takeover the most commonly reported identity fraud tactic in the sector, AI is adding another layer to the threat: 71% of payment and fintech companies say it is already being used to conduct fraud against them.
As AI moves beyond helping consumers search and compare products to actually making purchases on their behalf, the challenge goes beyond what the technology can do. Retailers and financial providers also need to establish who is acting, what they are authorised to do, and when the consumer needs to approve.
“We expect AI to play a bigger role this shopping season, helping consumers research and compare products, and find the best deals. Our research suggests that consumers are ready to give AI a bigger role in how they shop, but they still want the final say”, says Emma Bauer, Chief Product Officer at Signicat.

title: BBVA Uses AI to Better Understand Its Customers and Takes a Step Towards Developing a Foundation Model
summary:
BBVA's AI researchers have developed a model that interprets how customers interact with the bank's mobile app, providing a deeper understanding of their needs and paving the way for more personalized and proactive banking. The research, presented at ICAIF, a leading conference on AI applied to finance, marks another milestone in BBVA's efforts to lay the groundwork for an AI foundation model capable of integrating multiple data sources.
 








Every time customers use BBVA's mobile app, they perform a sequence of actions, whether checking their transactions, reviewing their cards, exploring loan terms or making a transfer, among many other possibilities. When analyzed together, these interactions provide valuable insights that can help optimize the bank's processes, improve the customer experience and deliver services better tailored to individual needs and interests.
Harnessing this information through AI is the goal of a research initiative that BBVA has been pursuing for almost a decade. Its latest milestone is a scientific paper developed by the bank's researchers and presented on November 15 in Milan at the ACM International Conference on AI in Finance (ICAIF).
Specifically, the paper was presented at a pioneering event held as part of the conference, dedicated to research into foundation and multimodal models for the banking sector.
A new approach to representing digital navigation
BBVA began exploring the use of embeddings in 2018. These numerical representations enable AI models to identify patterns and relationships within large volumes of data. In 2023, this research took another step forward by focusing on navigation data from the bank's app, transforming sequences of screens visited by customers into anonymized vector representations that can be reused by different analytical models.
This technology has already demonstrated its value in real-world applications at BBVA, such as customer segmentation and estimating the likelihood that a customer will take out a financial product. However, the approach used until now, based on Word2Vec, had an important limitation: although it could represent the screens visited, combining this information resulted in the loss of some of the context and sequence of interactions.
To overcome this limitation, researchers explored the use of Transformers, a deep learning architecture that makes it possible to analyze sequences and identify relationships between their elements, and which underpins large language models (LLMs).
The approach draws inspiration from natural language processing. Just as the meaning of a word depends on the words surrounding it, an action within the app can convey different information depending on the interactions that come before or after it.
In this case, each screen visited in the app is treated as a token, the basic unit of data that AI models read and generate, while the sequence of screens viewed during a session functions much like a sentence. Through self-supervised learning, the model learns to recognize navigation patterns directly from activity logs, without the need to manually label each sequence.
For this research, approximately 1.6 billion navigation sessions from eight million customers, covering one year of activity, were analyzed using anonymized data. Of these, 90 million sessions were selected to train the new models.
One of the main technical challenges was ensuring that this approach could operate at scale and adapt to an app that is constantly evolving. To address this, researchers developed a hierarchical tokenization system that groups related screens and makes it possible to interpret new features based on existing categories, avoiding the need to rebuild the system whenever the app changes.
Building on this foundation, different Transformer architectures were compared, with a decoder architecture ultimately selected. This architecture learns to predict the next screens in a sequence and combines contextual information from the entire navigation journey to generate a compact, reusable representation. As a result, each navigation session is converted into a vector that summarizes a user's behavior within the app. This vector can be used directly or combined with other sessions to obtain an overall representation of a customer's interactions.
From research to real-world banking applications
The results show that Transformer-based models outperform the previous technology by capturing navigation sessions more accurately and generating useful representations for analyzing customer interactions.
One of the most significant evaluations involved a model that estimates the likelihood of a customer taking out a financial product, a real-world use case already deployed at the bank. By incorporating the new embeddings, the AUC metric—which measures a model's ability to distinguish between customers who will take out a product and those who will not—increased by 2.7% in relative terms compared with the baseline model, also outperforming the result achieved with Word2Vec. This improvement is particularly significant given that the existing model already demonstrated strong predictive performance.
This improvement shows that using sequential models to interpret digital interactions provides additional information that can enhance the predictive capabilities of analytical models. Furthermore, the resulting representations can be reused across different models without requiring each one to process the customer's entire navigation history.
The solution is integrated into a process that serves approximately eight million active users and processes four million sessions per day, demonstrating its viability at scale while meeting requirements for efficiency, governance, reliability and maintainability.
Towards a foundation model that can learn from multiple data sources
The models developed so far focus on one specific dimension of customer behavior: digital navigation. However, much of a person's relationship with their bank is also reflected in other sources of information, ranging from transactions and account activity to interactions with relationship managers, phone calls and branch visits.
BBVA is already taking the first steps towards developing a multi-source foundation model capable of integrating these different dimensions and providing a foundation for building multiple AI applications.
Unlike models specialized in a single data source, this approach makes it possible to learn a comprehensive representation of BBVA customers' financial behavior from heterogeneous information. The goal is to move towards an intelligent, comprehensive and unified understanding of customers, providing a foundation for deploying AI models and agents across different use cases.
The research presented at ICAIF represents another step towards realizing this ambition. By combining scientific experimentation, accumulated knowledge and real-world deployment, BBVA is building a foundation for a new generation of AI models that can contribute to a deeper understanding of customers' needs and expectations, and to the development of banking that is increasingly personalized, proactive and people-centered.

title: ANZ Completes Major Cloud Data Transformation, Strengthening Data Foundations to Improve Customer Experiences
summary:
ANZ has completed the migration of one of its largest data platforms to Amazon Web Services (AWS), establishing a modern, scalable foundation to support the bank's growing use of data, analytics and AI.
The new cloud-based platform strengthens ANZ's ability to manage and protect customer information through enhanced security controls through a modern cloud architecture.
The Enterprise Big Data platform, which supports services across payments, business banking and customer remediation, was migrated from an on-premises environment to Amazon EMR, a managed cluster platform that simplifies running big data frameworks. The transformation moved 1.7 petabytes of data, equivalent to more than 340 million smartphone photos, across 300 million files, 142,000 tables, 4,500 automated data workflows and 4,000 views. 
The migration was completed in six months instead of an anticipated 18 months using AI-assisted engineering to help analyse, convert, test and optimise workloads. Engineers used a troubleshooting AI assistant powered by Amazon Bedrock to identify and fix performance bottlenecks using the chatbot, without needing to manually comb through code and configurations saving time.
By applying agentic AI across discovery and migration activities, ANZ reduced migration effort by an estimated 35 per cent compared with traditional approaches and reduced defects and rework by approximately 50 per cent through testing and validation. 
The new platform provides greater scalability and resilience while unlocking new opportunities to improve customer and employee experiences. 
ANZ Group Chief Information Officer Donald Patra said: "This transformation strengthens our technology foundations to make banking better and simpler for our customers. It also demonstrates how AI-assisted engineering can accelerate complex delivery while maintaining a disciplined focus on security, resilience and quality.”
A standout feature of the program was how ANZ and AWS Professional Services engineers used AI to accelerate delivery and improve outcomes.
The solution processed data at approximately seven times faster than an initial alternative approach, has already tokenised almost 80 terabytes of data and reduced operating costs from more than US$10,000 per day to less than US$3,000 per month.
ANZ Chief Data and AI Officer Kai Yang said: "Data is the foundation of modern banking and increasingly the foundation of AI. As we explore new ways to use data and analytics to improve customer and employee experiences, having modern, scalable and secure infrastructure is critical.
"This transformation modernises one of ANZ's most important data platforms and provides a stronger foundation for future innovation. It gives us greater flexibility to scale and simplify our technology environment and accelerate the development of new data and capabilities over time.
"Completing a program of this scale in six months demonstrates what can be achieved when technology, people and AI-assisted engineering come together behind a shared goal."
AWS Managing Director for Australia and New Zealand, Chris Casey said: "Migrating a major banking data platform while it continues to serve customers in real time is one of the most complex undertakings in financial services. Completing a migration of this scale in six months reflects the trust and world-class delivery capability of AWS Professional Services, AWS Partners, and the team at ANZ.
"It’s great to see ANZ using agentic AI to handle time-consuming processes that previously took months, giving the teams more time to focus on the complex work that needed expertise and human judgement."

title: BANCOMAT and CBI Sign an MOU to Build Italian Infrastructure Supporting the Digital Euro, With Nexi as Technology Partner
summary:
CBI, BANCOMAT and Nexi announce the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding for the launch of a strategic collaboration to build an Italian infrastructure supporting the digital euro, which will be developed with Nexi as technology partner. The solution will enable banks and Payment Service Providers (PSPs) to manage the processing of the digital euro, the issuance of which is subject to the ongoing legislative process, and connect to future Eurosystem services through a shared platform, with the objective of reducing investments and implementation costs, accelerating market entry, and streamlining technology upgrades.
The project aims to contribute to strengthening the competitiveness of the Italian financial system during a decisive phase for the evolution of European payments. The digital euro would complement cash as an additional form of money issued by the Central Bank and would be available to citizens, businesses, and public administrations within the euro area. 
The platform will be developed based on a shared, modular, and scalable infrastructure, in line with the European Central Bank’s roadmap and the evolution of the European regulatory framework. The goal is to foster adequate preparation among Italian operators and offer a coordinated response to a transformation set to impact the entire payments market.
The initiative combines the complementary expertise of the three organisations: CBI's experience in managing shared infrastructures and services for the financial sector; BANCOMAT's role as the national reference payment network; and Nexi’s established industrial and technological capabilities in digital payments across Europe.
Governance is entrusted to an equal partnership between CBI and BANCOMAT. Nexi will support the development of the solution as the technology partner, with contribution from TAS – an IT company specialised in payment solutions.
The infrastructure manages the connection of operators, the functions necessary for utilising the digital euro, and access to the central Eurosystem.
The model will be open, interoperable, and independent of individual technologies, with the aim of promoting service portability and accessibility even for smaller-sized operators.
For banks and PSPs, sharing the infrastructure will facilitate economies of scale, reducing costs, implementation risks, and the time required to offer new services. By streamlining activities, the shared platform can facilitate entry, especially for smaller operators, expanding competition and promoting the adoption of the digital euro.
“The digital euro marks a turning point for the European payment system. With this initiative, CBI is leveraging over thirty years of experience in building collaborative infrastructures to help banks and PSPs navigate change sustainably and effectively, in line with the path defined by the Eurosystem,” says Liliana Fratini Passi, Managing Director of CBI. “Italy can play a leading role. We want to combine skills, investments, and operational capabilities to equip the country with an open national platform capable of supporting the Italian market and contributing to the development of the digital euro in Europe.”
“The adoption of the digital euro will necessarily depend on the ability to involve those who operate daily on the ground, in direct contact with citizens and merchants, and to leverage already established payment networks and solutions,” states Fabrizio Burlando, CEO of BANCOMAT. “As systemic players, we have a duty to promote awareness of the new tool, favouring its integration into existing services and payment habits, and making its use simple. To this end, an effort is required from the entire payments sector so that the digital euro can become a practically utilised tool for citizens and businesses, enhancing its complementarity with solutions already present on the market.”
“The digital euro represents an important opportunity to strengthen the integration and competitiveness of the European payment system - says Bernardo Mingrone, CEO of Nexi Group - Nexi has always played a significant role in this journey, from the experiments promoted by the ECB to participation in the pilot, and up to network connectivity services: the collaboration with CBI and BANCOMAT constitutes a further contribution, putting our industrial and technological capabilities at the service of a shared solution that will facilitate the access of banks and financial operators to the future services of the digital euro.”
The MoU builds on established foundations, bringing together key players such as Intesa Sanpaolo together with isybank, the digital bank of the Group, which were among the first to join the project with BANCOMAT’s collaboration for technological aspects, as well as Nexi, which will use the platform for its direct merchants, and Poste Italiane, which, in addition to participating in the initiative, will make the Group’s cloud services available. The initiative, which is open to the entire banking and financial sector, has also attracted expressions of interest from a leading industry player, such as MPS. 
The platform has been designed with ambitions that go beyond national borders. It can be made accessible to European operators and integrated with other initiatives dedicated to digital currency and new payment instruments.
The collaboration between market infrastructures and technological enterprises thus offers Italy the opportunity to leverage its industrial expertise and contribute to building a more integrated and resilient European system.

content: BANCOMAT, CBI, and Nexi have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to build a shared Italian infrastructure supporting the digital euro. The initiative aims to help banks and Payment Service Providers manage digital euro processing and connect to future Eurosystem services, reducing implementation costs and fostering market competitiveness. The open, modular platform will involve key financial players and has ambitions to integrate with broader European payment systems.
content_ta: BANCOMAT, CBI மற்றும் Nexi நிறுவனங்கள் digital euro-வை ஆதரிக்கும் வகையில் இத்தாலிய உள்கட்டமைப்பை உருவாக்குவதற்கான புரிந்துணர்வு ஒப்பந்தத்தில் கையெழுத்திட்டுள்ளன. இந்த முயற்சியானது வங்கிகள் மற்றும் Payment Service Providers-க்கு digital euro செயலாக்கத்தை நிர்வகிக்கவும், எதிர்கால Eurosystem சேவைகளுடன் இணைக்கவும் உதவும். இதன் மூலம் செலவுகளைக் குறைத்து, சந்தைப் போட்டியை அதிகரிக்கச் செய்வதோடு, திறந்த மற்றும் மாடுலர் தளமாக இது செயல்படும்.
